runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for a children's dinosaur atlas, ages five to fourteen. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact anatomy, identity, composition, lighting, and background reference. Exactly one Tyrannosaurus rex remains on the right bank and exactly one Triceratops horridus remains on the left bank, always separated by the visible stream. Tyrannosaurus keeps one deep broad skull, two tiny two-fingered arms, two grounded hind limbs, and one complete heavy tail. Triceratops keeps two brow horns, one nasal horn, one solid frill, exactly four grounded legs, and one complete tail. After a brief hold, Tyrannosaurus performs one controlled non-contact bite feint: its deep head and short muscular neck move forward about three to four percent of frame width, the jaws open to a restrained natural gape and close once, while pelvis, feet, and tail remain planted. Triceratops lowers the rigid skull and frill six to eight degrees and braces without stepping. Both animals remain on their original banks, never overlap or touch, then settle. Fixed camera, fixed crop, stable trees, water, ground, shadows, color, and exposure; crisp readable anatomy in every frame. This non-graphic attack attempt is a generated ecological hypothesis, not direct behavioral evidence.
